relevance_note: Single-patient case report of a woman with a LAMP2 variant: "whole-exome sequencing (WES) demonstrated a heterozygous variant in lysosome-associated membrane protein 2 (LAMP2) gene (c.696T>A; p.Cys232Ter)".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). Relatives mentioned in Limitations (parents who died of non-cardiac diseases; a 27-year-old son described as healthy but not investigated) were neither tested nor affected and get no rows; 'no siblings'. Family history 'unremarkable' is not about the patient's own features. Age at diagnosis taken as 51 because the diagnosis was made by WES during the current admission of the 51-year-old (abstract: 'diagnosed with Danon disease late by genetic testing'); age at last evaluation also 51. Vital status not stated (later refusal of further information implies alive but is not stated). Variant type 'nonsense' taken from the paper's sentence that the variant changes cysteine to a stop codon (the sentence is attributed by the authors to ClinVar records); the word 'nonsense' is not used. Pathogenicity 'pathogenic' from the abstract. No parental testing (parents deceased), so inheritance not reported; the Discussion's general 'hemizygous' statement is about diagnosis in general, not this patient. Time-dependent findings: echocardiography 'showed a normal heart' in her 30s and three years before showed normal LV wall thickness, chamber size and EF, and troponin-T was normal then; at the current admission LV was slightly dilated with EF 51% and troponin-T markedly increased. These are recorded as separate excluded rows with the time point in severity_or_detail and are not treated as contradictions; checklist uses the current findings. General negatives recorded as written and not used to exclude specific checklist items: 'no heart murmurs or abnormalities of other systems found in physical examination' (only heart murmur excluded), 'EMG' negative (not used to exclude proximal muscle weakness), 'no ... other clinical manifestations of extracardiac impairment', 'isolated cardiovascular disease and was socially well-adjusted', 'no special medical or psychosocial record' (not used to exclude intellectual disability, myopathy, retinopathy etc.). No contradictions found. Note the NT-proBNP unit inconsistency in the paper (568 pg/mL vs reference 0–227 ng/L), copied as printed.
